_note: The topic vocabulary: one entry per chip on the news archive's filter, in the order the chips stand. Written by scripts/sync-news-notion.py out of the Themen multi-select on the Notion news database — its options, in the order they are dragged into there — and read by scripts/build-news.py, which draws a chip for each topic a post actually carries and a page per topic behind it. `slug` is that page's name, news-thema-<slug>.html, so renaming a topic in Notion moves its address. `en` is the English word AS IT STANDS INSIDE A SENTENCE — "8 posts on telemetry" — and the chip is the same word with a capital first letter, so one string covers both and the two cannot disagree; derived that way round because the other is lossy, "AI Act" lower-cased being "ai act". Notion has nowhere to keep it: a multi-select option is a name, an id and a colour, so the English word is the one thing on this page a person writes. A topic invented in Notion arrives here with `en` empty, which is a topic the vocabulary holds and the archive does not draw; the build refuses the day a published post carries it, rather than shipping a German chip and a half-German sentence to English readers. This lives beside content/news/ rather than inside build-news.py for the reason content/autoren.json does: what the company writes about is a fact about the company, not a change to a generator.
